title: Operations are not atomic across files, and nothing locks

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`jsonio.write` is atomic per file, but multi-file operations are not atomic across files.
`promote` and `apply_outline` write a slice then the index; a crash between leaves an
orphan slice or a `has_slice` mismatch — so `apply_outline`'s "write nothing at all"
docstring is not quite true. `purge` unlinks the file before saving the index. And two
`slicer add` processes both read `next_id`, mint the same id, and the later save clobbers
the earlier: no advisory lock anywhere.

Low frequency for a single user, but real for a team or an agent fan-out, and the
all-or-nothing promise should be honest.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/store.py` — an advisory lock around a load-mutate-save
- `src/slicer/ops.py` — ordering in `promote`, `purge`, `apply_outline`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. `apply_outline` that fails partway leaves no slice files (true all-or-nothing).
2. A held lock makes a second writer wait or fail cleanly rather than clobber.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
A file lock (`fcntl.flock` on a `.slicer/lock`, best-effort, stdlib) around the
load-mutate-save in the CLI entry, so concurrent writers serialize. Order writes so the
index is the last thing written, and in `apply_outline` stage slice writes so a mid-loop
failure leaves nothing. Keep it stdlib and degrade gracefully where flock is unavailable.

**Not in this slice:** a full transaction log or rollback — the lock plus write-index-last
covers the realistic cases.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: A simulated mid-`apply_outline` failure leaves the tree as it was.
